name: Cala Iris
hero_subtitle: Fishing village and park-coast gateway on the Al Hoceima National Park shoreline.

overview.title: Gateway to the park shore
overview.p1: Cala Iris is a small fishing settlement on the edge of Al Hoceima National Park — a practical base for beach time and for pushing further along the cliff coast.
overview.p2: The cove itself is modest; the value is the setting: park hills behind, Mediterranean ahead, and access to walks or boats toward wilder inlets.
overview.p3: Plan transport in advance. Combine with Torres de Alcalá when you want towers and wider views in the same outing.

q1.question: How far from Al Hoceima?
q1.answer: West along the coast — confirm current drive time with your driver.

q2.question: Is there a big resort?
q2.answer: No — expect a village-scale stop, not a built-up resort strip.

q3.question: Can I continue into the park?
q3.answer: Yes with local boats or guided walks when conditions allow.

q4.question: Food options?
q4.answer: Simple; carry snacks and water for longer park segments.

q5.question: Worth it without a boat?
q5.answer: Yes for the setting and a quieter cove day; boats unlock more of the cliff coast.
